about.title: Auburn Slip & Fall and Premises Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Falls happen fast, but the aftermath can drag on for weeks or months. Whether you slipped on a spill at a business near Rt 49, tripped on broken pavement along Auburn Folsom Road, or fell on a poorly lit staircase in a Placer County apartment complex, the days right after matter. California law generally requires showing the property owner knew, or reasonably should have known, about the hazard and didn't fix it or warn you. That's why photos of the hazard, witness names, and any surveillance footage from the property are worth gathering quickly, before video gets erased or the scene gets cleaned up. LawProactive doesn't practice law ourselves; we're a free service that connects injured Auburn residents with an independent personal injury attorney who can evaluate what happened, gather evidence, and deal with the property owner or their insurer on a contingency basis, meaning you owe nothing unless there's a recovery.

whyChoose.title: Why Auburn Residents Turn to LawProactive

items.title: Notice Is the Whole Case
items.desc: Because California requires proof the owner knew or should have known about the hazard, an attorney can help identify prior complaints, maintenance logs, or repeat incidents at the same Auburn property.

items.title: Video Disappears Fast
items.desc: Many stores and apartment complexes overwrite surveillance footage within days, so an attorney can move quickly to send preservation letters before that evidence is lost.

items.title: Comparative Fault Doesn't Have to Sink Your Claim
items.desc: Even if an insurer argues you weren't watching where you stepped, California's pure comparative fault rule still allows for a reduced recovery rather than none at all.

items.question: How long do I have to file a slip and fall claim in Auburn?
items.answer: In most cases, California gives you two years from the date of the fall to file a lawsuit. If the property involved is owned by a public entity, such as a city building or park in Placer County, the deadline is much shorter and requires an early claim. It's best to talk to an attorney soon so nothing is missed.

items.question: What if I fell at a store on Grass Valley Highway and no one saw it happen?
items.answer: Lack of witnesses doesn't end a claim. Many businesses along that corridor have interior surveillance cameras, and an attorney can request that footage be preserved before it's routinely deleted. Incident reports filed with store management can also help establish what happened.

items.question: Will I owe money upfront to talk to an attorney?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free connection service, and the independent attorneys in our network generally work on contingency, meaning they only get paid if you recover compensation. There's no cost or obligation to have your fall reviewed.
